title: Unbounded comparison: full faithfulness and sums
statement: Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the unbounded derived categories of ordinary module sheaves over the constant discrete ring $A$ on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the comparison geometric morphism $\nu_X$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Then its termwise inverse-image functor $\nu_X^*:D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ is exact and fully faithful and preserves arbitrary small direct sums.

source.place: Statement, consequence of the unbounded derived-unit isomorphism; proof sk-prop-pe-unbounded-classical-unit.proof.md

proof.text: Write $L=\nu_X^*$ and $R=\nu_{X,*}$ on module sheaves. The exactness of $L$ and the fact that its image consists precisely of classical sheaves are [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Thus termwise $L$ induces a triangulated functor on the unbounded derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The kernel/image computation in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^q(LK)=L H^q(K)$, so $LK$ has classical cohomology; it also identifies $L\tau_{\ge N}K$ with $\tau_{\ge N}LK$ naturally, by applying $L$ to the kernels and cokernels in the canonical truncation complexes.

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation: exactness and classical cohomology; Stacks 015F and 010N

proof.text:
The small-site module categories have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Termwise $R$ is additive, preserves chain homotopies, and commutes with shifts and the cone differential because it preserves finite biproducts; followed by localization it is therefore an exact functor from the homotopy category to the etale derived category. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to this functor gives $\mathbf R R$, computed on a K-injective representative $J$. Since $R$ is right adjoint to the exact $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $RJ$ K-injective. For a complex $P$ representing $K$ and $J$ representing $M$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give the natural chain of bijections
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(LP,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(LP,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(P,RJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(K,\mathbf R R M)$.
This constructs the unbounded adjunction $L\dashv\mathbf R R$. Its unit at $K$ is represented by $P\to RL P\to RJ$, where $LP\to J$ is the K-injective resolution and the first arrow is the sheaf-adjunction unit.

source.place: Setup of the unbounded unit; Stacks 079P, 070K, 070I and 08BJ

proof.text: Choose a K-injective $I$ representing $K$ and a K-injective resolution $LI\to J$; write $f:I\to RJ$ for its adjoint, representing the unit from Step 2. For an affine étale $W\to X$, restriction preserves K-injectives by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Identify the étale restriction with scheme inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], and the pro-étale slice with $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. These identifications apply to module actions and complexes termwise. Slice restriction is exact: kernels are sectionwise, and local lifts through an epimorphism over an object $V\to W$ are taken on covering arrows $V_i\to V$, which remain arrows to $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $(LI)|_W=\nu_W^*(I|_W)$. Thus $I(W)$ computes $R\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{ét}},K|_W)$ and $J(W)$ computes $R\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proét}},(LK)|_W)$, by the K-injective computation in Step 2. The defining formula $(RG)(W)=G(W)$ from [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] says that $f(W):I(W)\to J(W)$ is precisely the derived-section comparison: it is the unit followed by the resolution map. This construction is natural in $K$ and $W$, since the resolutions can be chosen functorially.

source.place: Cohomology sheaves as sheafified sections; Stacks 08FI and 04IX

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, the empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero, so both derived categories are zero and the assertion holds. Assume $X$ nonempty and put $e=2\dim X+1\ge0$. Fix an affine étale $W\to X$. For an $A$-module sheaf $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$, write $G_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ for its underlying abelian sheaf. The equation $\ell^a A=0$ makes $G_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ torsion. Apply clause (1) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds] to $G_{\mathrm{Ab}}$, $g=\mathrm{id}_X$ and the constant presentation of $W$: the abelian groups $H^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^{-1}G_{\mathrm{Ab}})|_W)$ vanish for $q>e$. By the abelian comparison [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] on $W$, the groups $H^q(W_{\mathrm{ét}},G_{\mathrm{Ab}}|_W)$ also vanish. The restriction/pullback identifications of Step 3 apply to the underlying sheaves as well. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget], the underlying group of the module-sheaf cohomology $H^q_A(W_{\mathrm{ét}},G|_W)$ is this same group; therefore that module cohomology vanishes. To identify the evaluation derived functors on $X$, choose an injective module-sheaf resolution $G\to E^\bullet$. Restriction is exact by its sectionwise slice description in Step 3 and preserves module injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. Thus $E^\bullet|_W$ is an injective resolution of $G|_W$, and its global-section complex is exactly $E^\bullet(W)$. Consequently $R^qF_W(G)=H^q_A(W_{\mathrm{ét}},G|_W)=0$ for $q>e$. Apply the finite-coefficient bounded-below section comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] on $W$ to $G|_W$ in degree zero to deduce $H^q_A(W_{\mathrm{proét}},(LG)|_W)=0$ for $q>e$. Every classical $A$-module sheaf is isomorphic to $LG$ by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], so the pro-étale bound applies to every classical module sheaf, exactly as required by [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation]. The etale bound says that the additive left exact evaluation functor $F_W:G\mapsto G(W)$ on module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ has $R^qF_W=0$ for $q>e$.

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation: bounds clause (1), abelian comparison 099W, module cohomology agreement 03FD, and bounded-below comparison

proof.text:
Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$ and choose $N<m-e-1$. The truncation triangle $\tau_{<N}K\to K\to\tau_{\ge N}K\to$ is the canonical one of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Apply [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound] (Stacks Tag 07K7) to $F_W$, using Step 4 and enough injectives from Step 2. Since $\tau_{<N}K$ has cohomology in degrees $\le N-1$, its derived sections vanish in degrees $>N-1+e$. In particular they vanish in degrees $m$ and $m+1$. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of the derived-section truncation triangle therefore makes
$H^mR\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{ét}},K)\to H^mR\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{ét}},\tau_{\ge N}K)$ an isomorphism. On the pro-étale side, Step 1 gives classical cohomology of $LK$, and Step 4 supplies the uniform classical bound. Clause (2) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation] makes
$H^mR\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proét}},LK)\to H^mR\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\tau_{\ge N}LK)$ an isomorphism. Identify the latter truncation with $L\tau_{\ge N}K$ by Step 1.

Use the square whose horizontal arrows are the degree-$m$ comparisons of Step 3 for $K$ and for $\tau_{\ge N}K$, and whose vertical arrows are induced by $K\to\tau_{\ge N}K$. It commutes by naturality of the unit and the resolution comparisons. Both vertical arrows are isomorphisms by Step 5. The bottom horizontal arrow is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], applied on $W$ to the bounded-below complex $(\tau_{\ge N}K)|_W$. This bounded-below hypothesis is unchanged by the exact restriction. Hence the top arrow is the composite of the inverse right vertical arrow, the bottom arrow and the left vertical arrow, and is an isomorphism. Equivalently $H^m(f(W))$ is an isomorphism for every $m$ and every affine étale $W$.

For the complexes of sheaves $I$ and $RJ$, form the presheaves $W\mapsto H^m(I(W))$ and $W\mapsto H^m((RJ)(W))=H^m(J(W))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], their sheafifications are $H^m(I)$ and $H^m(RJ)$: sections compute presheaf kernels and images, and exact sheafification carries their quotient to the sheaf kernel/image quotient. This is the elementary computation of Stacks Tag 0BKV, written here rather than attributed to the sheaf-only injective-acyclicity lemma. The affine étale objects are cover-dense by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]. Step 6 therefore makes the sheafified map $H^m(f)$ an isomorphism: local surjectivity follows on an affine cover, and any section in its kernel restricts to zero on that cover. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], the unit $K\to\mathbf R R LK$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology sheaves as sheafified sections and Conclusion; Stacks 03EI, 0BKV, 04HR and 05RT

proof.text: For $K,K'$ the adjunction of Step 2 sends $L(u)$ to $\eta_{K'}\circ u$. Step 7 makes composition with $\eta_{K'}$ bijective, with inverse composition with $\eta_{K'}^{-1}$, so $L$ is fully faithful. Both module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] supplies arbitrary small coproducts in their unbounded derived categories, including the empty coproduct. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the derived adjunction of Step 2 and a small discrete diagram shows that $L$ preserves those coproducts. Together with Step 1 this proves all three assertions.

source.place: Conclusion: full faithfulness and arbitrary direct sums; Stacks 079Q, 07D9 and 0038
